$comment: The platform's list of what it must not break — consumer-conformance.yml builds and tests
each entry against every platform PR touching src/**. A product that is not registered here
gets no protection, which is the incentive to register. Keep it small and honest: every entry
costs CI minutes on every platform PR, so mark a consumer 'conformance': false with a note
rather than deleting the signal that it exists.

consumers.note: Reference product for module, role, approval, document, and RAG seams. Consumes Plenipo.* alpha.28 from the vendored .packages feed.

Real Plenipo.* consumer (alpha.28), blocked on two prerequisites, both fixed in auditworthy#27: it repeated the platform version per csproj (the swap needs a central PlenipoVersion property), and it pinned Microsoft.Extensions.AI 10.7.0 while platform main requires >= 10.8.1, which is 12 NU1605 downgrade errors. Flip conformance on once auditworthy#27 merges.

Real Plenipo.* consumer (alpha.28) on main — src/Hireworthy.{AppHost,Host,Hiring} verified via the GitHub tree — and it filed #145 with an L3 reproduction, so it was consuming the platform while unregistered and therefore unprotected. Registered with conformance OFF deliberately, not as a judgement on the repo: #144 documents that one red consumer deadlocks every platform PR, so adding an unproven consumer to the blocking matrix while that is live would widen a known deadlock. Flip conformance on once #144 is fixed AND a manual build of Hireworthy.slnx against platform main is green.
Stale — still consumes pre-rename Cortex.* packages (alpha.14), so it would fail for reasons unrelated to any platform change. Upgrade tracked in casewell#40; re-enable once it lands.
Not yet a consumer on main — the foundations bootstrap is still on a feature branch. Flip conformance on once src/ with Plenipo.* references lands on main.
